rationale: The investigator's choice fits the evidence: the effectiveness question has randomised answers (claims c1 and c5), while the local unknowns are who stops reporting (claim c2), why (claim c3) and how alert response shapes it (claims c4 and c6). An explanatory sequential design first measures completion and alert response for every patient in the two running clinics, then interviews patients who stopped and triage nurses to explain the patterns, and integrates both strands in a joint display. Reporting follows GRAMMS.
alternatives: Pragmatic trial in the lung and head-and-neck clinics (withdrawn by the investigator: no equipoise after the rollout decision)
Completion data alone (refused: cannot explain why patients stop)
Interviews alone (refused: cannot show who stops or how often)
guidelines: GRAMMS (Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study)
whyNotMoreComplex: A convergent design with a comparison clinic would add nothing the timeline allows; the sequential design lets the quantitative findings choose whom to interview.

decision.statement: Evaluate the rollout with an explanatory sequential mixed methods design: completion and alert response data for all patients in the breast and colorectal clinics from March 2026 to February 2027, then interviews with patients who stopped reporting and with triage nurses, integrated in a joint display before the lung and head-and-neck clinics start.
decision.question: Who stops weekly symptom reporting, why, and how are alerts handled, before the programme reaches the remaining clinics?

criteria.text: Completion falls steeply in routine care and the fall follows unanswered alerts.
Patients link stopping to unanswered alerts, and weekend response is slow.
The rollout committee needs a local effectiveness estimate before offering weekly reporting to all patients.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval covering interviews with patients and triage nurses
gates.evidence: REB approval REB-ONC-2026-044 dated 2026-09-02, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Access to completion and alert timestamps from the reporting platform
gates.evidence: Vendor data agreement DA-2026-17, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Pragmatic trial of weekly reporting in the lung and head-and-neck clinics (withdrawn by the investigator)
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c2, c3, c4 and c6 from retrieved records; both gates rest on the investigator's approval records.

summary: Explanatory sequential mixed methods recommended; the decision rests on four ledger claims and both gates are met on the investigator's records.
